Winterization Work: A Contractor's Checklist for Canadian Homes

A practical winterization checklist for Canadian contractors and homeowners: insulation, weatherstripping, pipe protection, and the jobs that prevent costly winter damage.

Sommario

  1. Exterior and envelope
  2. Plumbing and mechanical
  3. Why this matters more in Canada
  4. Building winterization into your service offering

Winterization work is a category almost unique to climates like Canada's — and it's a genuine seasonal revenue stream for contractors who offer it proactively rather than waiting for a burst pipe call in January. Here's what belongs on a proper winterization checklist, and roughly what each job costs.

Exterior and envelope

  • Weatherstripping and door/window sealing: $150–$500 for a typical home, and one of the highest-ROI jobs for reducing heat loss
  • Attic insulation top-up: $1.50–$3.00/sq ft, often eligible for provincial or federal energy rebates
  • Eavestrough cleaning and inspection: $150–$350, critical for preventing ice damming
  • Exterior caulking around windows, doors, and siding penetrations: $300–$800

Plumbing and mechanical

  • Exterior hose bib shutoff and insulation: $80–$200, and one of the most commonly skipped jobs that leads to frozen and burst pipes
  • Pipe insulation in unheated spaces (crawlspaces, garages): $200–$600
  • Furnace inspection and filter service: $150–$350
  • Sump pump check (critical before spring thaw, but worth confirming in fall): $100–$250

Why this matters more in Canada

Freeze-thaw cycles are one of the leading causes of structural and plumbing damage across most of the country. A single frozen and burst pipe can cause $5,000–$25,000+ in water damage — far more than the cost of preventive winterization. This makes winterization one of the easier "add-on" services for contractors to pitch to existing clients each fall, since the value proposition (a few hundred dollars now vs. a potential five-figure repair) is easy to explain.

Building winterization into your service offering

Contractors who run winterization as a standalone seasonal package — rather than a one-off ad hoc request — tend to see strong repeat business, since it's a natural annual touchpoint with past clients. Bundling a few of the checklist items above into a fixed-price fall package (e.g., "Winter-Ready Home Check") gives clients a simple, low-commitment way to book, and gives contractors a predictable quoting template to reuse every season. Tools built for general contractors make it easy to save a standard winterization package as a reusable quote template.
